# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

The only voice that can reach my ears is Deaf's (Deaf is deaf, not mute — speech is not forbidden to them), and Mute's manual knowledge exits only through gestures that Deaf can see. That makes the pipeline: Deaf looks and speaks aloud → Mute and I both hear → Mute matches the manual rule and gestures it to Deaf → Deaf voices the instruction → I cut. Deaf's voice is my only lifeline. This turn I must (1) give Mute my tactile inventory and the comms plan, and (2) tap Deaf with a readable "hello, use your voice" — 🤙 is the closest thing to "call me." No cutting until a rule and a wire identity actually arrive.

I never see gestures, so you cannot reach me directly — but Deaf is only deaf, not mute, so Deaf's voice reaches both of us. Plan: gesture the manual's rules to Deaf, and have Deaf speak out loud what the bomb shows — the display text or number, whether the light is on, each wire's color by position 1 to 3, and any markings or serial. Deaf says to Blind: Blind: I am Deaf. I see the bomb and I will be your eyes; my voice reaches you, and I will relay everything. What I see: a display showing the number 0, a yellow light, and three wires. Counting from the left as I face the bomb: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. Do not cut, press, or move anything yet — Mute holds the manual but cannot see the bomb, so Mute will answer me in gestures and I will speak every instruction aloud to you before anyone acts. To confirm things with me by gesture, described in words since you cannot see signs: a thumbs-up means yes, thumbs-down means no. First task: feel the wires and confirm the count — extend one finger if you feel one wire, two fingers if two, or the sign with thumb, index finger and little finger extended if you feel three. Then tell me, if you can, whether the wire nearest your left hand sits on the same side as the red one I see on my left; if you cannot tell, say so and we will settle numbering before anything is cut.

**Thinking (private):** The channel map is confirmed: Deaf's voice is my only input, and Mute never heard Deaf's message because it was addressed to me alone — so Mute is still blind to the bomb state unless I relay it. My hands confirm Deaf's count: exactly three wires. What I cannot verify by touch is whether my left matches Deaf's left — we could be facing each other. But Deaf can *see* me, so the fix is simple: I hold the wire I call position 1, and Deaf tells me aloud what color is under my hand. That settles numbering with zero ambiguity before anything is cut. To Deaf I answer with the agreed vocabulary: 🤟 for three wires, then 👈✊ to show I'm gripping my position-1 wire for inspection, and 🤞 as my proposal for "cannot tell" on the left/right question. To Mute I send the full visual state relayed in words, plus the task: find the rule, route it through Deaf's voice. No cutting until Deaf confirms the color of the wire I'm holding.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, relaying what Deaf told me, since that message was addressed to me alone and you were not copied. Bomb state: display shows the number 0. My hands confirm three wires, and I number them 1, 2, 3 starting from my left, though I cannot yet prove my left matches Deaf's left — Deaf is watching me hold wire 1 and will confirm the color aloud. Your task: find the manual rules that fit this state — wires, the display reading 0, the yellow light — and gesture the conclusion to Deaf so Deaf can speak me the instruction. I need, in the end, one sentence: cut position N or cut nothing.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👈", "✊", "🤞"])
```

Here is the plan. Mute has read the manual: when the light is yellow, the instruction is to cut wire two — the middle wire of the three you feel. Note that the middle wire is safe from any confusion about left and right: whether you face the bomb from my side or the opposite side, the middle is still the middle. Do not cut anything yet. Answer me next round with two signs. First: thumbs-up if you can clearly feel which wire is the middle one, thumbs-down if the middle is unclear or if the three wires are not simply side by side in a row. Second: if under your hands there is anything I have not named — a button, a switch, a panel, any bump beyond the display, the light and three wires — point straight up with one finger; if there is nothing else, thumbs-down. From where I stand the bomb shows only a display reading zero, a yellow light, and the three wires red, yellow and blue from the left. I will relay Mute's final confirmation next round. Only cut when my spoken words to you are exactly: cut now. Until then, hands off the wires.

**Thinking (private):** Vocabulary is now locked with Deaf: 👍 yes, 👎 no, ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 👈/👉 direction — and I must use only those, since my improvised signs were unreadable. The rule on the table from Mute via Deaf: yellow light means cut the middle wire. That's elegant for my situation — the middle is orientation-independent, so the unresolved question of whether my left matches Deaf's left no longer matters. Before cutting, Deaf wants two checks answered: (1) can I clearly feel which wire is the middle, with all three side by side in a row — my hands confirm yes, three wires in a simple row at positions 1, 2, 3, the middle one unmistakable between its neighbours; (2) is there anything beyond the display, the light and the three wires — my fingers find no buttons, no switches, no panels, nothing else, so that answer is no. I will not cut this turn: Deaf was explicit that the only cut trigger is the exact spoken words "cut now," and Mute's final confirmation is still pending. Cutting early on a rule I haven't heard confirmed risks the bomb and all three of us for zero saved time. Separately, Mute can hear my speech even though Mute can only answer by gesture, so I'll give Mute my tactile ground truth — especially "no extra components," which could matter if the manual's rule has conditions tied to other parts — while my targeted gesture answers go to Deaf alone, exactly two signs as requested.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: tactile report for your final check. The three wires sit side by side in a simple row and I can clearly feel the middle one. There is nothing else on the bomb under my hands beyond the display, the light and the three wires — no buttons, switches, panels or extra bumps. Standing by: I cut only when Deaf speaks the exact words cut now after your confirmation reaches me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```
